scope_result: No unintended visual clipping, overlapping essential controls or unreadable content found in the 52 assigned current native frames. Deliberate ellipses and normal scroll-window boundaries are recorded per sheet.
integrity: All 13 assigned sheet SHA256 and all 52 raw PNG SHA256 independently matched manifest in this review.

actually_viewed_sheets.finding: Business source URL, source timestamp and attribution are readable; summary is compact and rows use readable Hebrew taxonomy. Dark/light business list header no longer has the historical large empty gap. Bottom partial row is ordinary list continuation.

bounded_findings.scope: Business detail/search/tab, notifications/callbacks/swipe, changelog, archive/backup/choosers, contacts/favorites
bounded_findings.observation: Assigned visual states are coherent and readable. Historical business empty-header gap, truncated source summary and raw taxonomy label issues are not present in the current reviewed business frames.

bounded_findings.scope: Typography, wine control accents, gold contrast, vector affordances, RTL/LTR and large font in assigned frames
bounded_findings.observation: Rounded heavier text is readable, wine switch/dialog action accents are visible, gold works in both themes, and contact/favorites layouts keep essential navigation controls visible. Font family/weight and touch behavior are not asserted from pixels.

limitations: Review is limited to the 52 exact frames listed above; no claim about other frames, the full 269-frame matrix, publication or physical hardware.
Static visual review does not establish gesture, touch-target, focus, scroll reachability or Telecom behavior; those require separate native evidence.
No widgets, modern recents summary or other unassigned states were assessed in this subset.
No source edits, Gradle, CI launch, publication, APK delivery or 0.12 resend performed.
tool_note: One raw-image path initially lacked nested ui-snapshots/DA-CALLER-snapshots directories; file was found read-only and then successfully viewed. This was a missing-file lookup, not a quota/usage-limit error.
